judged_text: The Salesforce service constructor now unconditionally performs a remote POST to login.salesforce.com plus a prisma.credential.update on every instantiation, whereas previously the connection was built from the stored token without any eager refresh or DB write. Every calendar operation that constructs the service (listing events, booking checks) now costs a network round-trip to Salesforce and a credential write even when the stored token is still valid; a transient Salesforce outage converts every read into an exception raised from object construction.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, new logic performs an OAuth refresh POST to `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` and then `await prisma.credential.update(...)` before returning a `new jsforce.Connection(...)`, with no conditional check for token expiry/validity. This means constructing/initializing the connection path now incurs a network round-trip and DB write and will throw on non-OK responses (`if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw ...`), matching the finding’s performance/availability concern. The diff doesn’t prove it happens literally inside a synchronous `constructor`, but it is clearly on the connection-creation path and is unconditional.
